s1.syndrome_frame: Acute skin lesions with vesiculobullous and pustular components on the hand
salient_findings: Vesiculobullous lesions on the dorsal aspect of the left hand
Extension of lesions to the palm and ventral aspect of the thumb
Presence of pustules on eroded areas
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 60s
History of hypertension and diabetes mellitus
Occupation as a butcher and occasional hunter
Contact with hares and rabbits
Lesions appeared on the left hand over 3 days
No fever or other systemic symptoms present
Fungal culture was negative
Bacterial culture showed Staphylococcus simulans
Polymerase chain reaction analysis for Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae was negative

shortlist.label: pustular psoriasis
shortlist.why_kept: presence of pustular lesions on the hand

shortlist.label: monkeypox
shortlist.why_kept: vesiculobullous lesions and contact with animals

shortlist.label: subcorneal pustular dermatosis
shortlist.why_kept: pustular lesions on the hand and absence of systemic symptoms

shortlist.label: neutrophilic dermatosis of dorsal hands
shortlist.why_kept: acute onset of skin lesions on the hand

raw.rationale: The patient's occupation as a butcher and hunter, with contact with hares and rabbits, and the appearance of hemorrhagic bullous lesions on the dorsal aspect of the left hand, are consistent with neutrophilic dermatosis of dorsal hands, which can be triggered by minor trauma or environmental factors.

rejected.label: pustular psoriasis
rejected.why: While pustular psoriasis can present with similar skin lesions, the patient's lack of systemic symptoms and the specific location of the lesions on the dorsal hand make it less likely.

rejected.label: monkeypox
rejected.why: Monkeypox typically presents with fever and systemic symptoms, which are absent in this patient, and the lesions are not characteristic of the disease.

rejected.label: subcorneal pustular dermatosis
rejected.why: This condition is rare and typically presents with superficial pustules, which do not match the patient's deep-seated lesions.

rejected.label: eosinophilic pustular folliculitis
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by follicular pustules, which are not present in this patient's case, and the lesions do not match the patient's presentation.
